title: mks@mkspi: ~
source: Output: the installer's real stage-1 output from Eitri's test rig (installer/rehearsal; a QEMU X-Plus 4 booted from a copy of a real printer's eMMC), build/rehearsal/logs/stage1-usb/stage1.log, 2026-10-22. Omitted: the development-bundle warning (a release has none). Composed from install.sh's own messages, because the rig used a backup made beforehand and supplied CONVERT on the command line: the two backup lines (backup_to_usb), the CONVERT prompt (confirm_typed), the progress page IP (empty in the rig) and the closing SSH line.

events.caption: The same checks as the dry run

out: ==> Checking that this is an untouched QIDI X-Plus 4
ok    board: QEMU virt as Firefly ROC-RK3328-CC (Eitri rehearsal)
ok    partition table: dos, /boot (256 MiB) + root (29024 MiB), label-id 0x6a783df4
warn  could not ask Moonraker whether a print is running; make sure the printer is idle
ok    free: 20.4 GiB on the stock root, 149.2 MiB on /boot; root uses 6.9 GiB
==> Fetching and verifying the Eitri release description
[eitri] using the release's static zstd (*** Zstandard CLI (64-bit) v1.5.7, by Yann Collet ***) - the stock system has none
MCU boards: not touched (--mcu skip). Both keep their stock firmware; the mainboard can be flashed later from the setup wizard.
New layout (the stock system stays bootable in p2):
==> A verified backup of the eMMC is required before anything is changed
Note: the image is a copy of the whole disk, so it holds your Wi-Fi password and QIDI account tokens. Keep it private.

events.caption: The backup to the USB stick: 5–10 minutes (shortened here)

out: ==> Backing up the whole eMMC to /dev/sda1 (vfat) - this takes 5-10 minutes
(This stick may also hold your QIDI QD_Update folder; the backup goes into EITRI-BACKUP/ and leaves it alone.)
==> Reading the backup back to prove it is intact
[eitri] data seed 0.0.0.dev0 (klipper): checksum, manifest, pinned firmware and unpack rules verified
skipped: MCU handling skipped by --mcu skip
==> Making sure the backup is still there

events.caption: Read this, then type CONVERT. Until now nothing has changed

out: Next the printer reboots into the Eitri installer. It will shrink the stock system, create new partitions
and write Eitri. Until it finishes, the stock system still boots; afterwards the original is kept in its
own partition and revert.sh switches back. Do NOT switch the printer off while the installer runs

events.prompt: Type CONVERT to continue, anything else aborts:
